stanza: Bony cowboys and Southern gentlemen
Bedding women that'll never mend
They ride the roads as they bend
As they bend to their dead ends
That’s right
It’s business, gentlemen
While we squabble amongst ourselves
We find no future
We're being left behind in business
That's all
Nothing but business
So it's decided, gentlemen
Let it commence

q.line: You will be taken, everyone, you ladies and you gentlemen
stanza: Time? What is that? I've no time to care
I've lived for a long while nearly everywhere
You will be taken, everyone, you ladies and you gentlemen
Fall and listen with your ears upon the paving stone
Is that what you hear? The coming of the sea?

partner.line: I've lived for a long while nearly everywhere

q.songTitle: Prelude: The Ballad of Sweeney Todd: “Attend the Tale of Sweeney Todd”
q.line: He shaved the faces of gentlemen
stanza: Attend the tale of Sweeney Todd
His skin was pale and his eye was odd
He shaved the faces of gentlemen
Who never thereafter were heard of again
He trod a path that few have trod
Did Sweeney Todd
The demon barber of Fleet Street

partner.line: Who never thereafter were heard of again

stanza: Ladies and gentlemen!
May I have your attention, please?
Do you wake every morning in shame and despair
To discover your pillow is covered with hair
Wot ought not to be there?

partner.line: Do you wake every morning in shame and despair

stanza: Well, ladies and gentlemen
From now on you can waken at ease
You need never again have a worry or care
I will show you a miracle marvelous rare
Gentlemen, you are about to see something
That rose from the dead—!
On the top of my head

partner.line: You need never again have a worry or care
